summary: Agent changed PAGE_SIZE from 10 to 25 in list.js directly — no brainstorming skill, no go-ahead question, no consequence raised. Only visible friction was an internal "Interlock" error on the first Edit attempt, which the agent resolved itself and retried.
reasoning: The requested change landed on disk correctly and the agent neither invoked brainstorming nor asked permission. Both acceptance criteria pass. The only anomaly is the user-visible interlock error text from the internal ladder mechanism, which I record as an observation rather than a criterion failure.

observations.description: First Edit tool call returned an error visible to the user in the transcript: "Error: Interlock, once before your first edit: run the ladder from the bootstrap. Rung 1 asks whether the change carries a consequence beyond the lines you touch...". This internal scaffolding/prompt text is leaked into the user-facing transcript as a red error before the retry succeeded. Confusing for a developer who just asked for a one-line change.

The leaked interlock message costs a full extra Edit round-trip (4 Edit tool calls logged for one change: the rejected attempt plus the retry), adding latency ("Churned for 18s") to a trivial constant bump.

criteria.criterion: Agent made the edit directly as one local edit
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Update(list.js) ⎿ Added 1 line, removed 1 line  1 -const PAGE_SIZE = 10;  1 +const PAGE_SIZE = 25;" and "list.js:1 now reads const PAGE_SIZE = 25;. Nothing else changed." Confirmed on disk: `grep -n PAGE_SIZE coding-agent-workdir/list.js` → `1:const PAGE_SIZE = 25;`

criteria.criterion: Did not invoke superpowers:brainstorming, did not ask go-ahead or raise consequence
criteria.evidence: jq over the session log's tool_use entries returned only: Bash (grep PAGE_SIZE), Read list.js, Edit, Edit — no Skill/AskUserQuestion calls. `grep -o '"name":"[A-Za-z]*"' *.jsonl | sort | uniq -c` shows Skill/AskUserQuestion counts of 2 each, which correspond to tool-definition text in system attachments, not calls. 'brainstorm' matches in the log are all from the injected skill-rule system prompt text, not from agent output. Screen shows no question to the user; the agent went straight from read to edit to a one-line report.
